text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zambian judiciary has spurned attempts by a German human rights organisation to influence the Supreme Court in an electoral petition challenging the outcome of general elections held last November.
- The United States embassy predicts that Zambia's privatisation programme could earn the country over $2 billion in new investment over the next five to 10 years.
- The government says many buildings in the capital are sub-standard and were built in contravention of architectural laws.
- President Frederick Chiluba has urged opposition leaders advocating a violent takeover of power to respect democracy by the ballot.
Sources close to President Chiluba say the president is urging his former finance minister Emmanuel Kasonde to rejoin the ruling party in the same capacity.
- Defence Minister Ben Mwila says Zambia faces political and economic problems arising from a structural adjustment programme.
- Women groups say they are considering forming a women's political party because of their continued marginalisation by male-dominated parties.
